artifact_role: Independent source-blind mathematical reconstruction of supplied Lean interfaces, not a semantic-match verdict
semantic_conventions: All unbound theorem parameters and displayed context types/typeclasses are universally quantified. Typeclass assumptions are part of each interface.

For normed real vector spaces, DifferentiableAt is ambient Fréchet differentiability. It asserts existence of a continuous linear derivative giving a first-order approximation with error o(||h||). It is not DifferentiableWithinAt.
fderiv is a total operator valued in continuous linear maps. At a nondifferentiable point it is the zero map. No totality caveat removes explicit DifferentiableAt hypotheses from a theorem interface.
ConvexOn ℝ S f includes convexity of S plus f(a x+b y)≤a f(x)+b f(y) for x,y∈S, a,b≥0, a+b=1. Convexity of S means a x+b y∈S for these choices.
StrictConvexOn ℝ S f includes convexity of S plus the strict inequality for x≠y and a,b>0 with a+b=1.
IsMinOn g S p is the comparison ∀z∈S, g(p)≤g(z). Feasibility p∈S is separate. It is global on the given S, not a merely local minimum.
Dψ(a,b) always uses derivative base b and displacement a-b. Fractional numerals in the concrete tests are real numbers.
No source/reference matching, proof correctness, successful Lean elaboration/compilation, or proof dependency is established by this reconstruction.

declarations.natural_language: For an arbitrary real-valued function on a real normed vector space, D at ordered arguments (x,y) is the function value at x minus the function value at y minus the total Fréchet-derivative operator at y applied to x-y. The second argument is the derivative base point, and the first is the evaluation point.

semantic_slots.objects_spaces: E is a type equipped with a normed additive commutative group and a real normed-space structure. Thus E is a real normed vector space; completeness, finite dimension and an inner product are not assumed. The codomain is the real numbers. The derivative operator has type E →L[ℝ] ℝ, a continuous real-linear map.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: The definition is available for every such E, every ψ:E→ℝ, and every ordered pair x,y∈E.
semantic_slots.assumptions: There are no regularity, convexity or set-membership hypotheses.
semantic_slots.conclusions: This is a definition of a real number, not a theorem asserting a distance property.
semantic_slots.constants_normalization: The coefficient of the derivative term is exactly 1. The derivative is evaluated at y and applied to x-y; there is no 1/2 factor or norm. fderiv is total: when ψ is not Fréchet differentiable at y it returns the zero continuous linear map, so in that case the defined expression is ψ(x)-ψ(y).
semantic_slots.probability_feedback: No randomness, probability space, observations, feedback protocol or stochastic quantification occurs.
semantic_slots.exclusions: No nonnegativity, symmetry, triangle inequality, positive definiteness, differentiability or existence of an optimization solution is asserted. Noncomputable is an elaboration/computability context, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.

declarations.natural_language: An exact three-point algebraic identity holds for arbitrary ψ and x,y,z: D(z,x)+D(x,y)-D(z,y) is the difference of the total derivative maps at y and x applied to z-x.

semantic_slots.objects_spaces: E is any real normed vector space. The subtraction on the right is subtraction in the space of continuous real-linear maps E→ℝ, followed by evaluation.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: Universal over ψ and all three points x,y,z, without a feasible set.
semantic_slots.conclusions: The displayed identity, with exactly the ordered pairs (z,x), (x,y), (z,y).

semantic_slots.exclusions: No derivative existence is implied. No inequality, nonnegativity, symmetry or norm/inner-product representation is asserted.

declarations.natural_language: If ψ is convex on X, both x and y belong to X, and ψ is Fréchet differentiable in the ambient space at the second point y, then the ordered value Dψ(x,y) is nonnegative.

semantic_slots.quantifiers: Universal over X, ψ, x and y satisfying the named assumptions.

semantic_slots.conclusions: 0≤Dψ(x,y), equivalently ψ(x)≥ψ(y)+dψ(y)[x-y] under the differentiability assumption.

declarations.natural_language: For a convex objective f on V, a positive real η, and an explicitly feasible global minimizer p of z↦f(z)+η⁻¹Dψ(z,x) over V, ambient differentiability of ψ at x and p implies the displayed bound for every feasible comparison point u. The reference point x need not be feasible.
declarations.latex: \begin{gathered}\eta>0,\ p\in V,\ \operatorname{ConvexOn}(\mathbb R,V,f),\ \psi\text{ Fr\acute echet differentiable at }x,p,\\\forall z\in V:\ f(p)+\eta^{-1}D_\psi(p,x)\le f(z)+\eta^{-1}D_\psi(z,x)\\\Longrightarrow\quad\forall u\in V:\ \eta\bigl(f(p)-f(u)\bigr)\le D_\psi(u,x)-D_\psi(u,p)-D_\psi(p,x).\end{gathered}

semantic_slots.objects_spaces: E is any real normed vector space; V⊆E; f,ψ:E→ℝ; η∈ℝ; x,p∈E. All functions are defined on the whole ambient E even though optimization is restricted to V.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: Universal over these data and proofs of the displayed hypotheses; the conclusion quantifies over every u:E with u∈V.
semantic_slots.assumptions: η>0; p∈V; ConvexOn ℝ V f, including convexity of V and its usual convex-combination inequality for f; ambient DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ x and DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ p. IsMinOn of g(z)=f(z)+η⁻¹Dψ(z,x) at p means ∀z∈V, g(p)≤g(z). It does not itself assert p∈V, which is separately supplied by hp.
semantic_slots.conclusions: For every feasible u, η(f(p)-f(u))≤Dψ(u,x)-Dψ(u,p)-Dψ(p,x). The conclusion is a deterministic comparison inequality conditional on the supplied minimizer.
semantic_slots.constants_normalization: The minimization objective has the reciprocal-step coefficient η⁻¹ multiplying D, and the conclusion has η multiplying the objective difference. η>0 ensures a nonzero reciprocal. Derivatives at x and p serve as the second-argument bases of the respective D terms. No derivative at u is assumed. The orientations and minus signs are exactly as displayed.
semantic_slots.probability_feedback: No randomness, noisy feedback, sampled gradient, iteration index or observation model occurs.
semantic_slots.exclusions: There is no assumption x∈V, no convexity or strict convexity assumption on ψ, and no differentiability assumption on f. V need not be open or closed. No existence or uniqueness of p is proved by this interface, no iterative convergence rate is stated, and no positivity of each individual D term follows from the listed assumptions alone. No inner product or completeness is required.

declarations.natural_language: In a complete real inner-product space, at a differentiability base point y the continuous derivative term defining D equals the inner product of the gradient at y with x-y.

semantic_slots.objects_spaces: E has a normed additive commutative group, a compatible real inner-product-space structure, and CompleteSpace E. Thus this declaration is over a real Hilbert space, potentially infinite-dimensional. The inner-product structure supplies the real normed-space structure needed by D. ψ:E→ℝ and x,y∈E.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: Universal over all such E and every ψ,x,y satisfying differentiability at y.
semantic_slots.assumptions: Ambient real Fréchet differentiability of ψ at y, together with the displayed complete inner-product-space typeclasses.
semantic_slots.conclusions: Dψ(x,y)=ψ(x)-ψ(y)-⟨gradient ψ y,x-y⟩ℝ. The gradient is the vector representing the continuous derivative by the real inner product.
semantic_slots.constants_normalization: The gradient is evaluated at the second point y and occupies the first inner-product argument. The displacement x-y is second. There is no scaling constant. Under hd this is the actual derivative representation, not an invocation of a fallback derivative at a nondifferentiable point.

semantic_slots.exclusions: No convexity, feasible-set membership, finite dimension, differentiability at x, or nonnegativity assertion is present. The displayed interface includes completeness and does not assert this representation for arbitrary normed spaces.

Zero globally minimizes z↦|z|+Dφ(z,1/2) over all real numbers: its value at zero is no larger than its value at every real z.
